stemMd: A survey asks whether respondents support a costly proposal to improve transport. A second survey asks about the same proposal without the word costly and finds greater support. The researcher says wording may matter. Which conclusion stays closest to the evidence?

options.label: C
options.textMd: Wording is the only possible cause under all circumstances.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Responses differed between the two wordings, suggesting a possible framing effect.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The second survey measured actual ticket purchases.

explanationMd: The observation concerns responses to differently framed questions. It suggests a wording effect, but without more design information does not prove wording was the only cause or predict actual behaviour.

distractorRationale.b: The surveys do not show universal opposition.
distractorRationale.a: Removing a word does not change the proposal's costs.
distractorRationale.c: Other design differences would also need to be excluded.
